interest: Japanese bids for Argentine submarines and coastal fishing rights.
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.20235, covering Japanese military, espionage, and propaganda activities in Argentina) consists of cross-reference sheets and an embassy despatch from 1933 to 1936 documenting American monitoring of Japanese strategic and commercial activities in the Southern Cone. The earliest documents note U.S. Navy Department intelligence regarding Japanese overtures to acquire an English meatpacking plant at Zárate and an offer to purchase three naval submarines from the Argentine government at a 30 percent markup over cost. The subsequent records, culminating in Tokyo Despatch No. 1670 from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew, examine Japanese press reports and diplomatic soundings regarding an Atlantic coast fishing concession obtained by Nippon Sangyo Kaisha through its subsidiary, the South American Fishery Company. While Argentine diplomats in Tokyo downplayed any official endorsement and noted the Ministry of Marine's strict resistance to foreign coastal concessions, they acknowledged the move as another persistent Japanese effort to secure a strategic foothold in South America.
